cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Management is a ____: The process of management is a series of continuous, composite, but separate functions
cards.back: Management is a continuous process: The process of management is a series of continuous, composite, but separate functions
cards.quote: Management is a continuous process: The process of management is a series of continuous, composite, but separate functions
reasons: review:Blank 'continuous process' leaks: the word 'continuous' still appears in the front ('continuous, composite...'), so the fill is given away.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Coordination, therefore, is not a separate function of management, but its very ____.
cards.back: Coordination, therefore, is not a separate function of management, but its very essence.
cards.quote: Coordination, therefore, is not a separate function of management, but its very essence.
reasons: review:Single blank 'essence' has obvious synonyms (core, heart); 'very ____' does not force one fill.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: How many main dimensions does management have (management is multidimensional)?
cards.back:
Three dimensions
Management is a complex activity that has three main dimensions.
cards.quote: Management is a complex activity that has three main dimensions.
reasons: review:Bare count 'three' without naming the dimensions; a student cannot use it. Weak, no testable point beyond a number.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Management is a continuous process. What does NCERT say about the five functions and who performs them?
cards.back:
Management is a continuous process
The process of management is a series of continuous, composite, but separate functions (planning, organising, directing, staffing and controlling). These functions are simultaneously performed by all managers all the time.
cards.quote: The process of management is a series of continuous, composite, but separate functions (planning, organising, directing, staffing and controlling). These functions are simultaneously performed by all managers all the time.
reasons: review:Front is open-ended ('what does NCERT say'); no single answer. Rework to ask who performs the functions and when.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Coordination integrates group efforts. What does this mean in NCERT?
cards.back:
Coordination integrates group efforts
Coordination unifies unrelated or diverse interests into purposeful work activity. It gives a common focus to group effort to ensure that performance is as it was planned and scheduled.
cards.quote: Coordination unifies unrelated or diverse interests into purposeful work activity. It gives a common focus to group effort to ensure that performance is as it was planned and scheduled.
reasons: review:Front 'What does this mean in NCERT?' is open-ended with no single right answer; ask for what coordination unifies.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Since all these qualities could not be found in a single person so Taylor proposed ____ specialists.
cards.back: Since all these qualities could not be found in a single person so Taylor proposed eight specialists.
cards.quote: Since all these qualities could not be found in a single person so Taylor proposed eight specialists.
reasons: review:Front has dangling 'these qualities' and never names functional foremanship, so it does not stand alone; add the cue.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What effect can each have on business: higher taxes, technological improvements, political uncertainty, changed consumer tastes?
cards.back:
Effects of environmental changes on business
Increase in taxes by government can make things expensive to buy. Technological improvements may render existing products obsolete. Political uncertainty may create fear in the minds of investors. Changes in fashions and tastes of consumers may shift demand in the market from existing products to new ones.
cards.quote: Increase in taxes by government can make things expensive to buy. Technological improvements may render existing products obsolete. Political uncertainty may create fear in the minds of investors. Changes in fashions and tastes of consumers may shift demand in the market from existing products to new ones.
reasons: review:Illustrative examples of environmental change, not a definition or headed list; four-part answer is not one answer.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is a pre-requisite for better business performance in the legal environment, and what can non-compliance of laws cause?
cards.back:
Knowledge of rules; result of non-compliance
Therefore, an adequate knowledge of rules and regulations framed by the Government is a pre-requisite for better business performance. Non-compliance of laws can land the business enterprise into legal problems.
cards.quote: Therefore, an adequate knowledge of rules and regulations framed by the Government is a pre-requisite for better business performance. Non-compliance of laws can land the business enterprise into legal problems.
reasons: review:Supporting line, not a definition or headed list; should be good, not must.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Planning establishes standards for controlling. What does NCERT say planning is for controlling?
cards.back:
A prerequisite
Therefore, we can say that planning is a prerequisite for controlling.
cards.quote: Therefore, we can say that planning is a prerequisite for controlling.
reasons: review:Answer "a prerequisite" has obvious synonyms (requirement, basis, necessity); no mark-carrying single fill.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: The next step is to weigh the ____ of each alternative.
cards.back: The next step is to weigh the pros and cons of each alternative.
cards.quote: The next step is to weigh the pros and cons of each alternative.
reasons: review:Synonyms (merits and demerits, advantages and disadvantages) fit equally; front does not name the step.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Besides quantifying plans, a budget is also what, from which deviations can be taken care of?
cards.back:
A control device
Thus, a budget is also a control device from which deviations can be taken care of.
cards.quote: Thus, a budget is also a control device from which deviations can be taken care of.
reasons: review:Answer "a control device" has synonyms (control tool, control measure, controlling technique); not one right fill.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: When a strategy is formulated, what must be taken into consideration, and what will affect an organisation's strategy?
cards.back:
Strategy and the business environment
Whenever a strategy is formulated, the business environment needs to be taken into consideration. The changes in the economic, political, social, legal and technological environment will affect an organisation's strategy.
cards.quote: Whenever a strategy is formulated, the business environment needs to be taken into consideration. The changes in the economic, political, social, legal and technological environment will affect an organisation's strategy.
reasons: review:Mild linking sentence rather than a headed point; should be good, not must.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: In a functional structure, what may practices that overemphasise one function's importance lead to?
cards.back:
Functional empires
Such practices may lead to functional empires wherein the importance of a particular function may be overemphasised.
cards.quote: Such practices may lead to functional empires wherein the importance of a particular function may be overemphasised.
reasons: review:Open-ended: many plausible answers (conflict, silos, rivalry); "functional empires" is not derivable from the front.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: NCERT: delegation does not mean what? The manager is still accountable for the assigned tasks.
cards.back:
Abdication
However, delegation does not mean abdication. The manager shall still be accountable for the performance of the assigned tasks.
cards.quote: However, delegation does not mean abdication. The manager shall still be accountable for the performance of the assigned tasks.
reasons: review:"Abdication" has obvious synonyms (abandonment, giving up responsibility); front is awkwardly two-part.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: For effective delegation, the authority granted must be what with the assigned responsibility?
cards.back:
Commensurate
Thus, for effective delegation the authority granted must be commensurate with the assigned responsibility.
cards.quote: Thus, for effective delegation the authority granted must be commensurate with the assigned responsibility.
reasons: review:"Commensurate" has obvious synonyms (equal, equivalent, proportionate, matching); not one right fill.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: The views of the ____ will be generally considered in the final selection
cards.back: The views of the concerned manager will be generally considered in the final selection
cards.quote: The views of the concerned manager will be generally considered in the final selection
reasons: review:Blank 'concerned manager' has near-synonyms (line manager, HR manager, manager); a student cannot know the exact fill from the front, and the point is low-value detail.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: ____: Very often, we find that individual objectives of employees and the organisational objectives as understood are conflicting to each other.
cards.back: Harmony of objectives: Very often, we find that individual objectives of employees and the organisational objectives as understood are conflicting to each other.
cards.quote: Harmony of objectives: Very often, we find that individual objectives of employees and the organisational objectives as understood are conflicting to each other.
reasons: review:front blanks only the principle heading; the sentence alone fits other names (Unity of objectives, Reconciliation); no cue that it is a principle of directing

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: ____: Mere giving of an order is not sufficient.
cards.back: Follow through: Mere giving of an order is not sufficient.
cards.quote: Follow through: Mere giving of an order is not sufficient.
reasons: review:front is one generic sentence ("Mere giving of an order is not sufficient") with a blank heading; many fills fit (supervision, feedback, follow through); no principle-of-directing cue

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: ____, social and ____ factors also play important role in providing motivation.
cards.back: Psychological, social and emotional factors also play important role in providing motivation.
cards.quote: Psychological, social and emotional factors also play important role in providing motivation.
reasons: review:blanks Psychological/emotional have obvious synonyms (cultural, economic); front lacks its subject (non-financial incentives) so is not standalone

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: When should actual performance be measured: after the task is completed, or during performance where possible?
cards.back:
During the performance, wherever possible
It is generally believed that measurement should be done after the task is completed. However, wherever possible, measurement of work should be done during the performance.
cards.quote: It is generally believed that measurement should be done after the task is completed. However, wherever possible, measurement of work should be done during the performance.
reasons: review:Supporting elaboration within the measurement step; should be good, not must.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Stability of Dividends: Companies generally follow a policy of ____ dividend per share.
cards.back: Stability of Dividends: Companies generally follow a policy of stabilising dividend per share.
cards.quote: Stability of Dividends: Companies generally follow a policy of stabilising dividend per share.
reasons: review:Blank 'stabilising' has an obvious synonym ('stable'); a student cannot know which form is the one NCERT prints, so the fill is not unique.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Borrowing at 10% with a tax rate of 30%: what is the after tax cost of debt?
cards.back: The firms in our examples are borrowing @ 10%. Since the tax rate is 30%, the after tax cost of debt is only 7%.
cards.quote: The firms in our examples are borrowing @ 10%. Since the tax rate is 30%, the after tax cost of debt is only 7%.

source.section: Factors affecting the Choice of Capital Structure

reasons: review:Worked-example arithmetic (10% borrowing, 30% tax gives 7%) taken from the illustration; not a definition, list, formula or fact worth memorising. Front is self-contained but the point is trivia.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Dividend decision: what contractual constraint can a lender impose on a company?
cards.back:
Contractual constraints
While granting loans to a company, sometimes the lender may impose certain restrictions on the payment of dividends in future. The companies are required to ensure that the dividend does not violate the terms of the loan agreement in this regard.
cards.quote: While granting loans to a company, sometimes the lender may impose certain restrictions on the payment of dividends in future. The companies are required to ensure that the dividend does not violate the terms of the loan agreement in this regard.
reasons: review:Front already names 'contractual constraint' and the back headline repeats it; the real answer (lender restrictions on dividend payment) is not what the headline gives. Reword to ask for the factor name.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: In what manner must the finance procured be invested, according to NCERT?
cards.back:
Returns must exceed the cost of procurement
Similarly, the finance so procured needs to be invested in a manner that the returns from the investment exceed the cost at which procurement has taken place.
cards.quote: Similarly, the finance so procured needs to be invested in a manner that the returns from the investment exceed the cost at which procurement has taken place.
reasons: review:Intro elaboration of financial management; should be good, not must.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What are speciality products?
cards.back:
Speciality products are those consumer goods
which have certain special features because of which people make special efforts in their purchase. These products are such, which have reached a brand loyalty of the highest order, with a significant number of buyers.
cards.quote: which have certain special features because of which people make special efforts in their purchase. These products are such, which have reached a brand loyalty of the highest order, with a significant number of buyers.
reasons: review:Quote starts mid-sentence on p258 ('which have certain special features...'), but back adds 'Speciality products are those consumer goods' (end of p257) that is not in the quote; back is not derived from quote. Quote must be the whole sentence across 257-258 and the card cited from 257. Definition-t

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What does the concept of product include beyond the physical product and its benefits (the extended product)?
cards.back:
Extended product
The concept of product also include the extended product or what is offered to the customers by way of after sales services, handling complaints, availability of spare parts etc.
cards.quote: The concept of product also include the extended product or what is offered to the customers by way of after sales services, handling complaints, availability of spare parts etc.
reasons: review:Front contains the term 'extended product' and the back headline repeats it; ask what the extended product covers or name it from its description.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Where are warehouses located for products needing long-term storage, such as agricultural products, and why?
cards.back:
Near production sites
For products requiring long-term storage (such as agricultural products) the warehouses are located near production sites. This helps in minimising the charges on transportation of the goods.
cards.quote: For products requiring long-term storage (such as agricultural products) the warehouses are located near production sites. This helps in minimising the charges on transportation of the goods.
reasons: review:Narrow fact on warehouse location; good, not must.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What do intermediaries do for the firm, in the place element of the marketing mix?
cards.back:
Activities of intermediaries
The intermediaries in turn keep inventory of the firm's products, demonstrate them to potential buyers, negotiate price with buyers, close sales and also service the products after the sale.
cards.quote: The intermediaries in turn keep inventory of the firm's products, demonstrate them to potential buyers, negotiate price with buyers, close sales and also service the products after the sale.
reasons: review:Open-ended front with a multi-item answer, headline only restates the topic; descriptive filler under the place element.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What does the marketing function of customer support services relate to?
cards.back:
Customer support services
A very important function of the marketing management relates to developing customer support services such as after sales services, handling customer complaints and adjustments, procuring credit services, maintenance services, technical services and consumer information.
cards.quote: A very important function of the marketing management relates to developing customer support services such as after sales services, handling customer complaints and adjustments, procuring credit services, maintenance services, technical services and consumer information.
reasons: review:Circular front ('customer support services' asked about itself); answer is a list, not one answer. Ask which marketing function covers after-sales, complaints, credit, maintenance.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: ____: It is the moral duty of any business to take care of consumer’s interest and avoid any form of their exploitation.
cards.back: Moral Justification: It is the moral duty of any business to take care of consumer’s interest and avoid any form of their exploitation.
cards.quote: Moral Justification: It is the moral duty of any business to take care of consumer’s interest and avoid any form of their exploitation.

source.section: From the point of view of Business

reasons: review:blank is a heading phrase; "moral duty" sentence also fits Ethical responsibility, Social responsibility; one right fill not derivable

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Which quality marks should a consumer look for on electrical goods, food products and jewelry?
cards.back:
ISI mark, FPO mark and Hallmark
Buy only standardised goods as they provide quality assurance. Thus, look for ISI mark on electrical goods, FPO mark on food products, Hallmark on jewelry, etc.
cards.quote: Buy only standardised goods as they provide quality assurance. Thus, look for ISI mark on electrical goods, FPO mark on food products, Hallmark on jewelry, etc.
reasons: review:back lead line "ISI mark, FPO mark and Hallmark" is composed, not an exact contiguous NCERT fragment; for a fact card use the NCERT sentence only

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the two business associations NCERT gives as examples that have laid down a code of conduct for their members.
cards.back:
FICCI and CII
The associations of trade, commerce and business like Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce of India (FICCI) and Confederation of Indian Industries (CII) have laid down their code of conduct which lay down for their members the guidelines in their dealings with the customers.
cards.quote: The associations of trade, commerce and business like Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce of India (FICCI) and Confederation of Indian Industries (CII) have laid down their code of conduct which lay down for their members the guidelines in their dealings with the customers.

source.section: Ways and Means of Consumer Protection

reasons: review:back lead line "FICCI and CII" is stitched from abbreviations, not an exact NCERT fragment; use the NCERT sentence only

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: To which body, and within how many days, can a party appeal against an order of the District Commission?
cards.back:
State Commission, within forty five days
If any of the parties are not satisfied by the order of District Commission can appeal against such order to the State Commission on the grounds of facts or law within a period of forty five days from the date of order.
cards.quote: If any of the parties are not satisfied by the order of District Commission can appeal against such order to the State Commission on the grounds of facts or law within a period of forty five days from the date of order.

source.section: Redressal Agencies Under The Consumer Protection Act

reasons: review:back lead line "State Commission, within forty five days" is composed, not an exact NCERT fragment; use the NCERT sentence only

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: To which body, and within how many days, can a party appeal against an order of the State Commission?
cards.back:
National Commission, within thirty days
If any of the parties are not satisfied by the order of State Commission can appeal against such order to the National Commission within a period of thirty days of such order.
cards.quote: If any of the parties are not satisfied by the order of State Commission can appeal against such order to the National Commission within a period of thirty days of such order.

source.section: Redressal Agencies Under The Consumer Protection Act

reasons: review:back lead line "National Commission, within thirty days" is composed, not an exact NCERT fragment; use the NCERT sentence only

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: To which body, and within how many days, can a party appeal against an order of the National Commission?
cards.back:
Supreme Court of India, within thirty days
If any of the parties are not satisfied by the order of National Commission can appeal against such order to the Supreme Court of India within a period of thirty days of such order.
cards.quote: If any of the parties are not satisfied by the order of National Commission can appeal against such order to the Supreme Court of India within a period of thirty days of such order.

source.section: Redressal Agencies Under The Consumer Protection Act

reasons: review:back lead line "Supreme Court of India, within thirty days" is composed, not an exact NCERT fragment; use the NCERT sentence only
